arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mohawk Industries argues that immediate appeals prevent inconsistent rulings on privilege.
Carpenter argues that finality rules must block immediate appeals of privilege orders.
Justice Sotomayor questioned if exceptions undermine the purpose of encouraging frank communication.
Justice Scalia asked if interlocutory appeals should exist for privilege issues.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether federal courts must allow immediate appeals of orders compelling disclosure of attorney-client communications. Mohawk Industries seeks to overturn a lower court's refusal to hear such an appeal. Carpenter defends the lower court's decision to deny the appeal.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute determines whether parties can challenge privilege orders immediately. It affects the consistency of federal court rulings on attorney-client secrets. It balances the need for finality against the risk of inconsistent privilege decisions.
